**Status:** completed

```sql
SELECT CAST(`pickup_zip` AS STRING) AS pickup_zip, COUNT(*) AS trip_count, ROUND(AVG(`fare_amount`), 2) AS avg_fare_amount FROM `samples`.`nyctaxi`.`trips` WHERE `pickup_zip` IN (10001, 10003, 10011) GROUP BY `pickup_zip`
UNION ALL
SELECT 'All 3 combined', COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(`fare_amount`), 2) FROM `samples`.`nyctaxi`.`trips` WHERE `pickup_zip` IN (10001, 10003, 10011)
ORDER BY trip_count ASC
```

Query returned 4 rows:

<!-- begin:query_17f55a -->
| pickup_zip | trip_count | avg_fare_amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10011 | 1129 | 10.91 |
| 10003 | 1181 | 10.98 |
| 10001 | 1227 | 10.62 |
| All 3 combined | 3537 | 10.83 |
<!-- end:query_17f55a -->

## Average fare for the top 3 pickup zip codes

Across all 3,537 trips from these zip codes, the average fare is **$10.83**. The three zip codes are within about $0.40 of each other. [Query Result](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/84cb39d7434e46c29b823d3f152d88c4?o=1234567890123456#embed-query_17f55a) [samples.nyctaxi.trips](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/samples/nyctaxi/trips?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=1234567890123456)

- **10003**: $10.98, the highest of the three
- **10011**: $10.91
- **10001**: $10.62, the lowest, even though it has the most trips

| pickup_zip | trip_count | avg_fare_amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10011 | 1129 | 10.91 |
| 10003 | 1181 | 10.98 |
| 10001 | 1227 | 10.62 |
| All 3 combined | 3537 | 10.83 |

The combined figure is an average over every trip, so zip codes with more trips count for more in it.
